item.title: Cisco Warns of New Zero-Day ISE Auth Bypass (CVSS 10.0) Exploited in Active Attacks
item.description: A maximum-severity auth bypass in Cisco's Identity Services Engine is being actively exploited, letting attackers skip login on a system that gatekeeps network access.

item.title: GPUHammer: Rowhammer Attacks on GPU Memories are Practical
item.description: Researchers show the Rowhammer bit-flip attack, long known on CPU memory, works practically against GPU memory too, threatening the integrity of GPU-accelerated computation.

item.title: Ransomware Incidents in Japan in the First Half of 2026
item.description: Problem: Japan saw 90 ransomware incidents in H1 2026, up 4.7%, with small and mid-sized firms making up most victims. Approach: Talos researchers picked apart open directories, leaked bash histories, and Python scripts left behind by two groups: The Gentlemen and Qilin. Result: The Gentlemen run a disciplined six-phase playbook: VPN access, Nmap/Masscan recon, a GLPI exploit, credential theft via Responder/Impacket, then AD lateral movement and cloud exfiltration, with Russian-language artifacts in their tools. Qilin's attack scripts show signs of being AI-generated: uniform doc-style headers and a stray "llm_chatbot" folder in its command history. Why it matters: Ransomware crews are professionalizing their tradecraft and now outsourcing script-writing to AI, shrinking the skill and time needed to build working attack tooling. Glossary: Lateral movement - moving between compromised systems inside a network. Exfiltration - stealing data out of a network. Active Directory - Windows' directory service for accounts and permissions. RaaS - ransomware sold as a subscription service to affiliates.

item.title: AMD presents new method of handing indirect lighting off to an image generation model: 'frame-by-frame' solution could be part of AMD's answer to DLSS 5 someday
item.description: AMD is generating indirect lighting frame-by-frame with an image model instead of computing it directly, a technique that could feed a future DLSS-style upscaler.

item.title: The lead developer of the PS5 Linux project has abandoned ship
item.description: The lead developer of the PS5 Linux homebrew project quit, criticizing contributors for leaning on LLM-generated code they don't understand, a friction point for AI-assisted reverse engineering.

item.title: Close-up images show defects locking electrons into stable Wigner solids
item.description: Physicists captured close-up images of crystal defects locking electrons into place as stable "Wigner solids," a rare ordered state driven purely by electron-electron repulsion.

item.title: Where Does the Quantum World End and Ours Begin?
item.description: Problem: Quantum objects behave like fuzzy waves that interfere with themselves, yet everyday objects have sharp, definite positions; physicists still lack a settled account of exactly where that switch happens. Approach: The piece surveys decoherence theory (environment scrambling quantum information), the "decoherent histories" reformulation that drops the need for an outside observer, and Leggett-Garg-style experiments testing whether a system had a definite property before measurement, pushed up to virus-sized molecules. Result: Every test so far still matches quantum mechanics exactly: interference survives even in large molecules, and it's the environment's bombardment, not a new law, that buries quantum effects at macroscopic scale. Why it matters: Pinning down this boundary experimentally shapes how far quantum computers can scale and what "measurement" really means. Glossary: Decoherence - environment destroying a quantum system's ability to interfere with itself. Superposition - existing in multiple states at once. Entanglement - distant particles staying correlated. Leggett-Garg test - experiment checking if a system had a definite state before measurement.

item.title: Plugin4Shell – Zero Click RCE Vulnerability found in top four coding agents
item.description: Researchers found a zero-click remote-code-execution chain affecting plugins in four popular AI coding agents, showing how agentic dev tools can be hijacked without any user action.

item.title: Flock cameras are riddled with security vulnerabilities and hard-coded credentials
item.description: An investigation found Flock's surveillance cameras full of vulnerabilities and hard-coded credentials, undermining a system already controversial for police license-plate tracking.

item.title: Goose: 1.16x faster than C++ and 1.12x than safe Rust, while memory safe
item.description: A new systems language claims to beat both C++ and safe Rust on benchmarks while keeping full memory safety, aiming to unseat manual memory management as the price of speed.
